analysis.title: Eli Lilly & Co. (LLY): Commercial Momentum Remains Uninterrupted
key_insights: LLY shares rose 6.6% (vs DRG 3.4%) after a third consecutive beat/raise this year. FY26 guidance has been raised by about $10bn cumulatively since the start of the year.
The $5.5bn guidance raise, from $85bn-$87bn to $91bn-$92bn, exceeded investor expectations of $90bn+ and drove much of the positive reaction, more than the quarterly beat did.
GS raises its FY26 revenue estimate from $89.8bn to $92.3bn and its EPS estimate from $32.77 to $35.89. New FY26/27/28 EPS are $35.89/$49.34/$56.78 vs prior $32.77/$46.08/$51.68.
12-month price target rises to $1,573 from $1,413 on an unchanged 28.0x Q5-Q8 PE multiple. Rating stays Buy, with 14.5% upside to the $1,373.70 close on 29 Oct 2026.

The stock is +27% YTD, but the move came from upward estimate revisions against a stable or contracting multiple, unlike the broader Pharma group, which saw multiple expansion. GS expects that dynamic to continue.
The two swing factors flagged at the start of the year, the Medicare Bridge program in the US and OUS Mounjaro strength, are both still playing out better than consensus has been modeling.

Medicare Bridge GLP-1 program (started July 1) continues to propel Zepbound volumes. Per LLY, 80% of Bridge patients are new to incretin starts, 75% of seniors choose injectable therapy, and 7 of 10 (about 500k+ patients as of Sept) pick a LLY medicine. LLY expects the tailwind to continue through 2027+.

CMS data from October shows the Bridge program has reached 1.1mn patients vs LLY's prior framing of a 20mn Medicare TAM, though GS notes the comparison may not be like for like. GS's KOL survey points to more than 7mn patients on therapy by July 2027. Every 1mn Bridge patients is about $2.9bn of revenue in GS's model, and the 2027 Medicare channel forecast stays at $8bn.

GS cites panelists from its Washington policy trip who think a Bridge extension beyond 2027 looks likely. LLY management pointed to a health policy paper estimating substantial savings from the program.

OUS Mounjaro beat VA consensus by 9% again. The OUS incretin analogs market grew 53% in Q3 with LLY holding almost 60% share. OUS Mounjaro reaches only 2 of every 100 eligible patients, vs 1 in 10 in the US. LLY says it is holding or growing share even after generics launched in India, Brazil and Canada.
GS raises its OUS Mounjaro FY26 estimate 2.6% from $21.0bn to $21.6bn. It sees consensus, which implies 1-2% sequential growth, as overly conservative.

Foundayo came in slightly light in Q3, its second quarter of launch. New patients doubled vs Q2, about 4 of 10 patients starting an obesity medicine choose it, and 25% of patients are on a maintenance dose, which LLY says is higher than Novo's oral Wegovy pill. GS cuts its FY26 Foundayo estimate 21% from $710mn to $561mn.

Foundayo is launched OUS in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, the UK and Mexico, with a global rollout across all major markets (40 additional countries) planned for 2027. Management sees the oral expanding the market rather than cannibalizing existing therapies.
Next-generation obesity commentary was consistent with prior framing. LLY has multiple long-acting incretin efforts in the clinic and is deciding which to advance to Phase 3.
Kisunla beat consensus by 10% with q/o/q momentum as bottlenecks ease. The TB-3 trial, a key Phase 3 event in 2027, could support expansion to earlier-stage Alzheimer's.

GS sees the EMBER-4 readout for LLY's oral SERD imlunestrant in breast cancer as an underappreciated potential blockbuster catalyst not reflected in consensus. Management says its trial is more robust and more relevant to real-world practice than competitor studies from Roche and AZN.
The December 7 R&D day is the next catalyst. The company says it will focus on under-the-radar pipeline assets.

FY26 model changes: Mounjaro +2.3% to $40.8bn, Zepbound +1.6% to $20.1bn, Jardiance +19.6% to $4.8bn, Trulicity +4.3%. SG&A comes in 5.6% below the prior estimate and adjusted EBIT ex acquired IPR&D rises 6.5% to $48.2bn.

market_movers.rationale: Price target raised from $1,413 on higher estimates after the 3Q26 beat/raise, using an unchanged 28.0x Q5-Q8 PE. Incretin volume gains are expected to offset pricing headwinds, and EMBER-4 is flagged as an underappreciated catalyst.

earnings_insights: LLY 3Q26: third consecutive beat/raise this year. FY26 company revenue guidance raised to $91bn-$92bn from $85bn-$87bn (a $5.5bn raise), vs investor expectations of $90bn+.

GS FY26 estimates (post-print, revised): revenue $92.3bn (prior $89.8bn), adjusted EPS including acquired IPR&D $35.89 (prior $32.77). GS FY27 EPS $49.34 (prior $46.08), FY28 EPS $56.78 (prior $51.68).
OUS Mounjaro in 3Q26 beat VA consensus by 9% (reported). Kisunla beat consensus by 10% (reported). Foundayo was slightly light vs GS and consensus forecasts in its second launch quarter.
GS product estimates for FY26 (GS forecasts, not reported): Mounjaro $40.8bn (US $19.2bn, OUS $21.6bn), Zepbound $20.1bn, Foundayo $561mn (cut from $710mn), Verzenio $5.9bn, Jardiance $4.8bn.
GS quarterly EPS estimate for 9/26E is $7.49 and for 12/26E is $11.49, shown in the GS forecast table.
Upcoming catalyst: December 7 R&D day. In 2027 two key Phase 3 events turn over in the non-incretin franchise, including the EMBER-4 readout.

trade_ideas.description: Buy LLY, 12-month price target $1,573 on a 28.0x Q5-Q8 PE multiple
trade_ideas.rationale: Upward estimate revisions against a stable multiple, continuing incretin volume momentum, and Phase 3 catalysts including EMBER-4.
trade_ideas.risk: A greater-than-expected annual pricing decline in the obesity market, lower share from competition or execution, and worse-than-expected pipeline data.

risk_factors: A greater-than-expected annual pricing decline in the obesity market.
Lower-than-expected market share from external competition or internal lack of execution on current and pipeline assets.
Worse-than-expected pipeline data could cut medium-to-long-term estimates and lead to multiple compression.
Uncertainty over whether the Medicare Bridge program is extended beyond 2027 and what trends look like after the initial bolus of patients.
Foundayo is ramping slower than GS and consensus forecasts, with the two lower doses still 75-80% of total prescriptions.

tension_points.bull_case: Volume tailwinds from the Medicare Bridge program and OUS Mounjaro continue to offset the pricing headwinds already built into GS's model, supporting further estimate raises on a stable multiple.
tension_points.bear_case: A greater-than-expected annual pricing decline in the obesity market, or lower share from competition or execution, would pressure estimates. Bridge volume after the initial bolus and a possible extension past 2027 are also unresolved.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A greater-than-expected annual pricing decline in the obesity market.

theme_stances.key_argument: The Bridge program is driving strong US Zepbound volumes from Medicare patients mostly new to incretin therapy, which expands the market.
theme_stances.evidence: Medicare patients that were mostly naive to incretin therapy

theme_stances.key_argument: OUS Mounjaro keeps beating consensus, and consensus growth assumptions look overly conservative given low penetration.
theme_stances.evidence: breadth and depth of the cash pay international weight loss market

theme_stances.key_argument: The EMBER-4 readout is an underappreciated catalyst for a potential blockbuster oral SERD in breast cancer that consensus does not reflect.
theme_stances.evidence: underappreciated catalyst for a potential blockbuster opportunity in breast cancer
